brief.situation: 11:20 in a family practice. You are the nurse practitioner. Mr. Brooks, 61, walked in because his lower lip swelled up this morning. He has taken lisinopril for five years and asks for 'an allergy pill' so he can get back to work.
handover: Hypertension and type 2 diabetes. No new foods, stings or medicines. No itch, no hives.

Practice policy: any swelling of the tongue, throat or voice, or difficulty breathing, means 911 for transport to the emergency department; the practice has oxygen and an emergency kit, not an airway team.
The hospital is 15 minutes away by ambulance.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each assessment takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings are telling you.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Mr. Brooks's tongue is swelling and his voice is muffled. What is happening, and what do you do?

parts.label: What is happening
parts.criteria: Swelling without hives or itch on an ACE inhibitor, even after years, is ACE inhibitor angioedema (bradykinin); antihistamines, steroids and epinephrine often don't work; tongue and voice involvement means the airway is at risk.
parts.modelAnswer: This is ACE inhibitor angioedema even after five years: no hives, no itch, bradykinin-driven. Antihistamines won't fix it, and now it's in his tongue and voice, so his airway is at risk.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: 911 now for the emergency department; sit up with oxygen; stay with him; stop the ACE inhibitor permanently and record it; hand off.
parts.modelAnswer: Call 911 now, keep him sitting up with oxygen and stay with him, stop the lisinopril for good and record it, and hand off to the crew.

scoring.modelReasoning: Lip swelling without hives or itch in a patient on an ACE inhibitor is ACE inhibitor angioedema, even after years on the drug. It is bradykinin-driven, so antihistamines, steroids and epinephrine often don't help. The drug is stopped for good and recorded, and he stays sitting up with oxygen ready. When the tongue swells and his voice changes, the airway is threatened: 911 now.

choices.label: It is driven by bradykinin, not histamine
